To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) UAV tracking is a challenging task that requires a new benchmark and (2) the best trackers for UAV tracking are the ones that are designed for low altitude aerial videos.

(i) state-of-the-art trackers do not perform well on aerial video sequences and that (ii) the performance of a tracker on aerial video sequences is highly dependent on the type of UAV and the camera used to capture the video.
the best performing trackers on our benchmark are DSST, TLD, KCF, and MEEM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two important aspects of UAV tracking: 1) the evaluation of existing trackers and 2) the development of a simulator to facilitate future work in this area.

(1) the development of a benchmark to evaluate the performance of existing trackers in the challenging UAV domain; (2) the creation of a simulator to generate realistic UAV tracking datasets and evaluate trackers in simulated environments before they are deployed “in the field”.
three main contributions: a benchmark dataset, a simulator, and a thorough experimental evaluation of state-of-the-art trackers on UAV videos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best trackers for UAV tracking are the ones that are able to cope well with scale variations and motion blur, while also being able to run in real-time.

, in the context of the benchmark, the best performing trackers are the ones that are able to deal with the challenges of aerial videos and UAV tracking, such as the high frame-rate, the low altitude perspective, the high camera motion, and the small target size, and that, in the case of the simulator, it can be used to test and evaluate tracking algorithms in a real-time scenario, and generate synthetic tracking datasets with automatic annotations.
the benchmark and simulator can be used for evaluating the performance of object trackers in a real world scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a benchmark for the UAV tracking community and a simulator for the development of tracking algorithms for UAVs.
we propose a new benchmark and a simulator for UAV tracking, and we show how the proposed benchmark and simulator can be used in practice.
the benchmark is a new dataset for low altitude UAV tracking and the simulator can generate new synthetic tracking datasets with automatic annotation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UAV tracking is significantly more challenging compared to traditional camera setups and that the performance of many popular trackers drops drastically in this new setting.
UAVs provide a unique and challenging perspective for target tracking, which is different than that of a ground camera and requires a re-thinking of existing tracking methods.
the performance of many popular trackers degrades in the aerial perspective.
